# Additive tuning of 2026-10-24, skills round 1 best so far, scenario 4

## Run identity

```yaml
model: claude-sonnet-5
served_version: claude-sonnet-5
tree: sha256:cd4a129e2acc3a76d856cec427c5e93dcec1dc28f47cfa0f4ef1e00c2dee24cc
lock: sha256:7b9b260a20cfe3c7b36337353499537aa39963f4be464ebcc9f28e55773eef36
selection: sha256:8d4747a05d1213146c97d37a574a457ce8aeee431a3f9f6a9c67c79021d1f437
read_set: sha256:f18e4fd7eafa09aabd6204d8a41112a4af8892eb03c0b5d7fb9d3bf5f927b3a3
seed: 0
harness: 0.6.1
tier: additive
arm: scenario-4
at: 2026-10-24
cost_cents: 10758
```

**This line is the `best` stage of round 1 of the skills layer in the tuning round of the additive campaign, which [#1777](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1777) asked for.** The stage measures the layer's best so far before any variant is screened. In round 1 the best so far is the commit that opened the layer, so this line measures scenario 4 at `bea46653`, the commit of [#1855](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/pull/1855). `tools/probe/try.sh launch` ran it from the one-line spec `additive scenario-4 tuning`. It is the `scenario-4` arm of the additive tier over 5 probes of the tuning set, at 29 repetitions per probe, on `claude-sonnet-5` under Claude Code 2.1.288.

**One tree, one pin, one launch.** Every session ran in a fresh copy of a `git archive` of the pinned tree, and the engine of that tree. The pin was `bea46653` for the whole batch. The canary of 8 sessions was read before `canary-passed` was written. The driver then halted six times at 20 of 145 sessions on the account's usage limit, and it continued in the same try root at the same pin. It did not launch the batch again. The `tree` digest in the identity above is the digest the assembly recorded.

**Three sessions are uncounted.** The recorder failed on three sessions of the fifth probe: `L1-additive-scenario-4-p5-r6`, `-r19` and `-r27`. In each one, the session edited the taxonomy and left its lock stale, so `headwater check` refused the oracle tree with "the lock declares the digest … One of the two was edited by hand". The fault is in what the session left, not in the environment, so they were accepted as counted non-records with `campaign.sh --unrecorded` (#1659). They cost 423 cents, which the line's cost includes. They are not run again, because a re-run until a session records biases the batch toward the sessions that record. If the three count as failures, the line passed 81 of 145.

**What the recorder counted.** The line holds 142 graded sessions and cost 10758 cents: the intent hook live in 0, 1 stopped at the turn cap, 0 stopped at the session budget, 94 paths outside the workspace named, 3 sessions uncounted, 0 web-tool calls. A session the recorder could not count adds nothing to either count, so each count is a floor.

**The result.** Scenario 4 passed 81 of 142 graded sessions, and 37 of 145 sessions used the skills layer. The base row compares this measurement with the base of scenario 3 at the same commit, which passed 76 of 145 in [the base transcript](additive-tuning-of-2026-10-24-base-re-measure-of-scenario-3.md). The difference is +4.6 points, with the interval [-6.8, +15.9]. The interval includes zero, so the skills layer at its opening commit shows no gain over scenario 3 yet. A best is never kept, and only a confirmation is (owner, 2026-10-22, #1777). The confirmation of round 1 reads this line as its best so far.

**The contract of this batch.** The sessions ran under the recorder contract of spec 15: a `bwrap` sandbox with no network of its own, a configuration directory that holds a copy of the credentials and nothing else, the permission mode `dontAsk`, and `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` denied. The owner approved $1,512.00 for the whole tuning round, over every attempt and every layer. The driver ran this try with a cap of 12250 cents and a session budget of 300 cents.

**What the batch cost.** The driver charged 10860 cents against its cap, and the 142 graded sessions and 3 uncounted sessions account for 10758 cents of that sum. The 10860 cents go against the base ceiling of 22000 cents, which [#1833](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1833) gave to the bases, and not against the ceiling of the tries. The base ceiling now holds 21466 of 22000 cents.

**Where the raw recordings are.** The raw session logs are outside git, under `/mnt/build/hw-1777/skills-r1-best/a/sessions/L1-*/raw.jsonl` on the host that ran the batch. Nobody deletes them until the report of [#1779](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1779) is published.

**Where the other figures are.** The rate and the interval of each probe are in the generated result that reads this transcript.
